title: Food Allergies in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Fourteen allergen categories are compulsory, everywhere, including the Imbiss.** Annex II of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 sets the list, and in Germany it covers unpackaged food too: restaurants, bakery counters, market stalls and canteens all have to be able to tell you.

**The counter may answer out loud, but only if a written record exists.** Under § 4 of the German LMIDV of 5 July 2017, oral allergen information is lawful only where a written or electronic record is immediately available on request and a visible notice says so. Asking to see it is a right, not a favour.

**Celery and mustard are the two nobody sees coming.** Suppengrün and stock powder put celeriac into most German soups and sauces, and mustard sits inside sausage meat, remoulade and potato salad. Between them they touch about half the classic Berlin plates.
**Glutenfrei is a legally capped word, at most 20 mg/kg.** Regulation (EU) No 828/2014 also defines sehr geringer Glutengehalt at 100 mg/kg. A spoken "probably fine" carries none of that weight.

**A printed Spuren von line is the weakest signal on the label.** Trace warnings are voluntary and have no legal threshold behind them, so they tell you far less than the fourteen mandatory declarations do.
**Say the sentence, then ask for the paper.** Two lines get you further in Berlin than any restaurant list: name your category in German, then ask whether the allergen information exists in writing.
